events.title: An encounter before its public afterlife
events.summary: David Fravor later described seeing an unusual object during a Navy training deployment near the USS Nimitz.
events.significance: The encounter, its later testimony and the release of related footage are different events.
established: Fravor’s 2023 statement records his own visual account; another crew subsequently captured infrared footage.
limitations: The account alone does not independently establish the object’s performance or origin.

events.title: The story reaches the front page
events.summary: The New York Times published its Pentagon UFO-program story online December 16; it appeared on the print front page December 17.
events.significance: A useful starting point for the modern public chronology.
established: Contemporaneous coverage identifies the reporting and print appearance; ABC separately obtained a Pentagon statement about the program.
limitations: Coverage of a program is not confirmation of an extraordinary explanation.

events.title: The Navy standardizes UAP reporting
events.summary: ODNI’s later assessment dates the Navy’s standardized reporting mechanism to March 2019.
events.significance: Reporting procedures affect what enters the official record.
established: A formal reporting mechanism is documented retrospectively in the 2021 assessment.
limitations: More reports need not mean more unusual objects.

events.title: The Pentagon formally releases three videos
events.summary: The Defense Department authorized release of three already-circulating Navy videos: FLIR, GIMBAL and GOFAST.
events.significance: Official release clarified provenance without settling interpretation.
established: ABC reproduced the Pentagon statement describing one November 2004 recording and two from January 2015.
limitations: Authorization to release unclassified footage is not confirmation of anomalous motion or non-human origin.

events.title: A dedicated UAP task force is approved
events.summary: The Pentagon announced on August 14 that the UAP Task Force had been approved August 4.
events.significance: UAP reporting gained a designated defense coordination body.
established: Contemporaneous reporting quotes the department’s task-force announcement.
limitations: Creating an investigative office does not establish what reported objects are.

events.title: ODNI publishes its preliminary assessment
events.summary: The assessment examined 144 reports; one was identified with high confidence as a balloon.
events.significance: It made both the reporting problem and the limits of available data explicit.
established: ODNI described a heterogeneous dataset, including reports from multiple sensors.
limitations: Unresolved reports are not a count of extraordinary craft. Incomplete data can prevent identification.
openQuestions: Which cases have enough calibrated, contextual data for competing explanations to be tested?

events.title: Grusch’s earlier inspector-general disclosure
events.summary: The Debrief later reported that David Grusch provided information to the Defense Department inspector general in July 2021.
events.significance: This predates his public allegations.
established: The chronology is reported from interviews and documents described by the journalists.
limitations: The confidential submission itself was not independently inspected for this page.

events.title: A separate intelligence-inspector-general complaint
events.summary: The Debrief described a May 2022 complaint concerning alleged concealment and reprisals.
events.significance: The complaint is distinct from later interviews and testimony.
established: The publication reported the complaint’s existence and timing.
limitations: A complaint’s procedural treatment is not a finding that alleged non-human craft exist.

events.title: UAP returns to an open congressional hearing
events.summary: Defense officials Ronald Moultrie and Scott Bray appeared before a House Intelligence subcommittee.
events.significance: The subject entered a public oversight forum.
established: The official transcript documents the hearing and officials’ testimony.
limitations: A hearing is a forum for scrutiny, not a certification of every statement made.

events.title: NASA announces an independent UAP study
events.summary: NASA announced a study of how to investigate UAP with available and future data.
events.significance: It framed the problem around scientific methods and data quality.
established: NASA’s public chronology documents the study announcement.
limitations: The announcement was not a conclusion about any reported object.

events.title: AARO succeeds the task force
events.summary: ODNI’s annual report records the establishment of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office.
events.significance: The defense effort expanded into a standing, cross-domain office.
established: The establishment date and succession are documented in the ODNI report.
limitations: An office’s mandate is not evidence for a particular origin hypothesis.

events.title: Grusch’s recovery-program allegations become public
events.summary: The Debrief published Grusch’s claims about concealed recovery and reverse-engineering programs.
events.significance: The claims gave oversight a specific alleged subject to investigate.
established: The article records his allegations and others’ supporting statements.
limitations: It does not publicly authenticate recovered non-human technology.

events.title: Schumer and Rounds propose a disclosure framework
events.summary: The senators announced an NDAA amendment proposing a UAP records collection and an independent review process.
events.significance: This was a legislative proposal, not enacted law.
established: The sponsors’ release documents what they introduced.
limitations: Introduction does not establish chamber passage or enactment; later law must be read separately.

events.title: Grusch, Graves and Fravor testify
events.summary: The House heard testimony from David Grusch, Ryan Graves and David Fravor.
events.significance: It placed distinct kinds of accounts into a public oversight record.
established: Grusch’s prepared statement attributes recovery-program information to others; Fravor described his own encounter.
limitations: Sworn testimony is evidence of an account, not independent verification of its explanation or of alleged recovered material.

events.title: NASA releases its study-team report
events.summary: NASA’s independent team set out ways to improve UAP data collection and analysis.
events.significance: The recommendations offer a testable research agenda.
established: The report emphasizes better observations and reproducible analysis; it found no conclusive extraterrestrial evidence in the peer-reviewed literature considered.
limitations: This was not a comprehensive resolution of military case files.

events.title: A UAP records collection becomes law
events.summary: The enacted FY2024 NDAA required a UAP records collection at the National Archives.
events.significance: A statutory records process is different from a proposed disclosure regime.
established: Public Law 118-31, sections 1841–1843, provides collection and disclosure procedures, including grounds for postponement.
limitations: The law does not certify the truth of allegations in records or guarantee immediate, complete disclosure.

events.title: AARO issues its historical review
events.summary: Reuters reported that AARO found no evidence that a government investigation had confirmed extraterrestrial technology.
events.significance: This records the office’s historical assessment.
established: The reported finding is an institutional conclusion.
limitations: It does not identify every unresolved object. The original report PDF was inaccessible during this audit.

events.title: The House holds another UAP hearing
events.summary: Tim Gallaudet, Luis Elizondo, Michael Gold and Michael Shellenberger appeared before House Oversight subcommittees.
events.significance: The hearing continued public scrutiny of transparency and UAP claims.
established: The committee’s hearing page establishes the date and witnesses.
limitations: The hearing’s title and the witnesses’ participation do not validate every underlying allegation.

events.title: AARO reports a larger caseload
events.summary: DefenseScoop reported 757 additional reports in AARO’s annual analysis.
events.significance: Report counts describe the intake system, not a census of anomalous craft.
established: The article documents the annual report and the director’s accompanying briefing.
limitations: Counts mix reporting periods and older submissions. Unresolved cases and incomplete data remain.

events.title: AARO’s director testifies to the Senate
events.summary: Jon Kosloski described AARO’s work and unresolved cases to a Senate Armed Services subcommittee.
events.significance: The director’s assessment is available in a public primary record.
established: His statement says AARO had found no verifiable extraterrestrial evidence while some cases still required investigation.
limitations: An institutional assessment is not a case-by-case demonstration that every observation has been explained.

events.title: The National Archives releases its first collection records
events.summary: NARA announced records from the FAA, NRC, ODNI and Office of the Secretary of Defense.
events.significance: This is a dated, documented implementation of the records law.
established: The release notice identifies the initial contributing agencies and continuing transfers.
limitations: Collection membership does not authenticate every account or establish that all responsive records have arrived.

events.title: Oversight focuses on transparency and whistleblowers
events.summary: The House held a hearing titled Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection.
events.significance: It continued the public oversight record.
established: The official page lists the hearing and witnesses, including Dylan Borland and Jeffrey Nuccetelli.
limitations: Witness testimony remains attributed; holding a hearing does not adjudicate its claims.

events.title: Trump announces plans to release UFO files
events.summary: Reuters reported that President Donald Trump said he would direct agencies to identify and release relevant records.
events.significance: This documents a public executive intention.
established: The report records the announcement, rather than an inspected executive order.
limitations: It is not evidence that all records were immediately declassified or that alleged non-human origins were confirmed.

events.title: The first PURSUE file release
events.summary: DefenseScoop’s reporting identifies May 8 as the first PURSUE release.
events.significance: It opened another route to public records and imagery.
established: The publication describes the released material and interviews researchers and officials about its limits.
limitations: Raw files can lack decisive context. The official portal was inaccessible to this audit; no independent analysis of every file is claimed.

events.title: A later annual assessment is reported
events.summary: DefenseScoop described AARO’s FY2025 annual report in July 2026, including 319 new reports.
events.significance: The report year, release period and observation dates are different.
established: The article dates its reporting to July 21 and says the report was released that week.
limitations: An exact release day was not verified. Inconsistent component counts in the article are not reproduced.

events.title: A plan to access a private historical archive is reported
events.summary: DefenseScoop reported that the Pentagon sought access to a large civilian UFO archive.
events.significance: The proposed access would broaden the historical material available to investigators.
established: The article describes an intended base year with four optional years.
limitations: This is not evidence of a contract award. The notice’s exact date was not verified from readable procurement text.

events.title: A restricted disclosure waiver is announced
events.summary: The department announced relief for certain disclosures to designated PURSUE representatives.
events.significance: A protected reporting channel is different from permission to disclose publicly.
established: The reproduced announcement describes civil and administrative relief under specified secrecy agreements for this channel.
limitations: The operative signed waiver was not inspected. Do not infer blanket public-disclosure permission, criminal immunity or confirmation of any allegation.

events.title: A sixth PURSUE release is reported
events.summary: FOX 5 DC reported another Pentagon release of historical and contemporary UAP files.
events.significance: The public record continued to grow after the first release.
established: The dated coverage documents the release announcement.
limitations: The inaccessible original manifest prevents an independently verified file count here. Releasing a record does not validate its explanation.

events.title: NASA’s study team meets in public
events.summary: NASA’s independent UAP study team held a public meeting on May 31, 2023.
events.significance: Public deliberation preceded the final research recommendations.
established: NASA’s meeting notice and retrospective caption document the meeting.
limitations: This establishes a public scientific meeting, not an identified origin for UAP.

events.title: Leonardo studies birds and the mechanics of flight
events.summary: Leonardo da Vinci’s Codex on the Flight of Birds is dated to 1505–1506 in Smithsonian’s account.
events.significance: An early example of observation-led flight research, included as scientific context.
established: The manuscript concerns bird flight and proposed human flight.
limitations: This source supplies no connection to UFO technology, NHI or later classified programs.

supports: compilation range and subject of the codex

events.dateNotes: A compilation range, not a precisely dated experiment or successful aircraft.

events.title: Brown Brothers Harriman takes shape
events.summary: The firm’s chronology dates the combination of Brown Brothers and the Harriman banking businesses to 1931.
events.significance: Establishes which business is being discussed before later financial claims are compared.
established: BBH’s own history places Prescott Bush’s private-client work in the combined firm.
limitations: An interested institutional history is not an incorporation filing. BBH and Union Banking Corporation must not be treated as the same legal entity.

supports: Prescott Bush role and retrospective date qualification

events.dateNotes: Year-level date. Merger negotiations and the operational combined firm should not be assigned an invented common day.

events.title: Einstein signs a warning about nuclear chain reactions
events.summary: Albert Einstein signed a letter to President Roosevelt, prepared with Leo Szilard’s help, urging attention to nuclear research.
events.significance: Connects scientific advocacy to the later wartime atomic program through a specific document.
established: DOE’s chronology dates the letter to August 2, 1939.
limitations: Signing this letter does not establish that Einstein worked on the Manhattan Project or supplied an exotic propulsion theory.

events.title: The Office of Strategic Services is established
events.summary: A military order established the OSS under the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
events.significance: Clarifies the wartime organization associated with William Donovan and later intelligence histories.
established: NARA dates establishment to June 13, 1942, and abolition to October 1, 1945.
limitations: The OSS did not simply become the CIA under a new name; intermediate organizations and transfers intervened.

events.title: The Army creates the Manhattan Engineer District
events.summary: An Army order created the district that administered the atomic-bomb project.
events.significance: Places nuclear weapons development in a documented wartime structure.
established: DOE gives the order date; NARA records an August 16 effective date.
limitations: This administrative record establishes no link to recovered craft.

supports: August 16 effective date and later transfer

events.dateNotes: Order August 13; effective August 16, 1942. These are different administrative dates.

events.title: The Alien Property Custodian vests Union Banking shares
events.summary: Vesting Order 248 covered all 4,000 shares of Union Banking Corporation and specified associated indebtedness.
events.significance: Provides a contemporaneous legal record for a frequently conflated part of Bush–Harriman financial history.
established: The shareholder table lists Prescott S. Bush with one registered share. The Custodian found the shares were held for a Rotterdam bank controlled by members of the Thyssen family.
limitations: Registered and beneficial ownership are different. The order concerns UBC, not a seizure of BBH itself; it does not demonstrate a UFO program or establish every director’s knowledge or intent.

supports: scope, execution date, registered shares and attributed beneficial-ownership finding

events.dateNotes: Executed October 20; filed November 6; published November 7, 1942.

events.title: John G. Trump examines Tesla’s papers, according to PBS’s history
events.summary: PBS recounts a government examination of Nikola Tesla’s papers after his death, with an assessment by electrical engineer John G. Trump.
events.significance: Separates a documented historical lead from claims that the papers yielded extraordinary working weapons.
established: The account quotes Trump’s negative assessment of workable new principles in the material he examined.
limitations: The underlying file was not directly inspected in this audit. A review of papers does not establish a functioning device, a transfer to UFO research or access to every Tesla record.
events.dateNotes: Only the year of the examination is assigned here; no exact examination or public-release day is inferred.

events.title: An intelligence report recounts the Maison Rouge meeting
events.summary: SHAEF report EW-Pa 128 relayed an informant’s account of an August 10 meeting at Strasbourg’s Rotes Haus, or Maison Rouge.
events.significance: Makes the surviving report, its provenance and its evidentiary limits inspectable.
established: The report describes industrial and military figures discussing postwar economic arrangements and underground activity.
limitations: It is not a meeting transcript or independent verification of implementation. It does not establish a gathering of “14 bankers,” or a chain connecting the meeting to UFO programs.

supports: report date, attributed meeting date and reported participants

events.dateNotes: The timeline sorts on the surviving report date. Its State Department covering dispatch is dated November 27, 1944.

claimDate.attribution: Informant account relayed in SHAEF EW-Pa 128
claimDate.note: Reported meeting date; occurrence and details are not independently established by this report alone.

events.title: Trinity inaugurates the nuclear-test era
events.summary: The Manhattan Project conducted the Trinity atomic test in New Mexico.
events.significance: Provides a firm reference point for later claims about nuclear facilities and unusual observations.
established: DOE’s chronology records the test on July 16, 1945.
limitations: Proximity in time or geography is not evidence that nuclear testing caused UFO activity.

events.title: The Atomic Energy Act creates the AEC
events.summary: The Atomic Energy Act established the civilian Atomic Energy Commission.
events.significance: Identifies the successor responsible for atomic administration after wartime Army control.
established: Manhattan District assets transferred to the AEC on January 1, 1947.
limitations: Creation by law and transfer of operations are separate; neither establishes possession of non-human technology.
events.dateNotes: Statutory date August 1, 1946; transfer date January 1, 1947.

events.title: Kenneth Arnold reports objects near Mount Rainier
events.summary: Pilot Kenneth Arnold reported nine objects near Mount Rainier.
events.significance: A prominent starting point for the postwar “flying saucer” reporting wave.
established: NARA’s history identifies the date and reported observation.
limitations: Estimated speed and the objects’ origin are not calibrated measurements established by this historical summary.

events.title: Roswell’s flying-disc announcement is followed by a balloon explanation
events.summary: Roswell Army Air Field announced recovery of a “flying disc”; the military then described balloon debris.
events.significance: The contemporary announcement is distinct from later claims about a crash, bodies or retrieval programs.
established: GAO’s records review reproduces and discusses surviving 1947 records.
limitations: The announcement does not authenticate an extraterrestrial craft. This date is the announcement date, not a proven crash date.

supports: July 8 announcement, subsequent explanation and surviving records

events.title: The National Security Act reorganizes national defense
events.summary: The 1947 act provided the framework for the National Security Council, CIA and a separate Department of the Air Force.
events.significance: Helps readers distinguish organizations that recur in later intelligence and UFO records.
established: NARA identifies the law and the agencies’ different establishment arrangements.
limitations: The law’s existence provides no evidence for a hidden UFO mandate.

supports: Department of the Air Force establishment

events.dateNotes: The July 26 law and September implementation dates are not treated as interchangeable.

events.title: The CIA begins under the new national-security framework
events.summary: NARA gives September 18 as the CIA’s effective establishment date under the July 26 act.
events.significance: Places later CIA-held records within the correct institutional chronology.
established: The Central Intelligence Group preceded the CIA.
limitations: A document’s presence in CIA files does not establish CIA authorship, endorsement or a successful operation.

events.title: The Air Force orders Project Sign
events.summary: An Air Force order initiated a formal UFO study effort.
events.significance: Begins the institutional sequence later associated with Grudge and Blue Book.
established: NARA dates the Sign order to December 30, 1947, and describes its later inconclusive assessment.
limitations: The order date is not a finding that the reported objects had an exotic origin.

events.title: Project Blue Book follows Sign and Grudge
events.summary: The Air Force ordered Project Blue Book in March 1952, following its earlier Sign and Grudge studies.
events.significance: Names successive investigations without treating them as one unchanged program.
established: NARA’s chronology identifies the sequence and month.
limitations: An investigation establishes official attention, not the explanation for every case.

events.title: A State Department memo records WCC’s Donovan connection
events.summary: A memorandum discussed a World Commerce Corporation steel-mill proposal and identified General Donovan’s law firm as its representative.
events.significance: Supplies a specific documented business relationship instead of an inferred intelligence network.
established: The contemporaneous memo identifies WCC president Frank Ryan and the representation in this matter.
limitations: It neither establishes WCC’s exact formation date nor proves OSS ownership, an intelligence mission or a UFO connection.

supports: WCC proposal, named president and Donovan law-firm representation

events.dateNotes: Date of the memorandum; this is not presented as WCC’s founding date.

events.title: The National Security Agency is established
events.summary: A presidential memorandum dated October 29 established the NSA effective November 4.
events.significance: Distinguishes the signals-intelligence organization from other agencies and similarly named archives.
established: NARA records both authorization and effective dates.
limitations: Its existence does not authenticate every intercepted or filed account.
events.dateNotes: Authorization October 29; effective November 4, 1952.

events.title: ARPA is established for advanced defense research
events.summary: Defense Secretary Neil McElroy established the Advanced Research Projects Agency, later called DARPA.
events.significance: Adds the research institution often invoked in accounts of unusual aerospace technology.
established: DARPA’s history dates establishment to February 7, 1958, in the aftermath of Sputnik.
limitations: An agency’s research remit is not evidence that a particular speculative technology worked.

events.title: The Space Act creates NASA
events.summary: The National Aeronautics and Space Act established NASA; transfers from NACA took effect October 1.
events.significance: Distinguishes civilian space research from military and intelligence organizations.
established: NARA records the act and the later transfer date.
limitations: Space exploration is relevant context; its existence is not evidence of contact.
events.dateNotes: Law July 29; operational transfer October 1, 1958.

events.title: A Defense directive establishes the DIA
events.summary: DoD Directive 5105.21 established the Defense Intelligence Agency.
events.significance: Identifies the institution later associated with military remote-viewing programs.
established: NARA records the August 1 directive.
limitations: This date is the directive, not an independently verified start date for every DIA operation.

events.title: A letter sets out a covert National Reconnaissance Office
events.summary: A Defense–CIA agreement described an office to manage satellite and aerial reconnaissance.
events.significance: An original record of compartmented human reconnaissance work supplies concrete context for secrecy.
established: The letter specifies proposed management, collection responsibilities and cover arrangements.
limitations: The documentary edition warns that the co-directorship did not take effect as written. The record does not establish an exotic vehicle program.

supports: dated letter, office remit and editorial qualification

events.title: The Air Force announces the end of Blue Book
events.summary: The Air Force announced termination of Project Blue Book.
events.significance: Closes a major public investigation while leaving its surviving records available for later scrutiny.
established: The Air Force said the investigation had found no evidence of extraterrestrial vehicles or a national-security threat.
limitations: That institutional assessment is not a case-by-case resolution of every unidentified report.

supports: termination date and attributed Air Force conclusions

events.dateNotes: Announcement December 17, 1969; NARA’s separate history places the end of operations in January 1970.

events.title: Robert Monroe publishes his out-of-body account
events.summary: Robert Monroe’s Journeys Out of the Body appeared in 1971, the year the institute’s history also associates with its creation.
events.significance: Provides a dated entry into the Monroe/Gateway strand of consciousness research.
established: The 1983 Army assessment cites the book; the institute describes its own development.
limitations: An autobiographical account is not a controlled demonstration. The institution’s historical labels do not establish an exact incorporation date.
events.dateNotes: Year precision only. The source’s 1971 creation language and “since 1973” wording are not collapsed into an invented exact founding day.

events.title: CIA begins research on remote viewing
events.summary: AIR’s later program review dates the beginning of CIA remote-viewing research to 1972.
events.significance: Establishes that government-backed investigation occurred, independently of whether the proposed ability worked.
established: The review describes a succession of sponsors and research and operational efforts.
limitations: Funding and classified handling do not validate paranormal mechanisms. This entry is a retrospective program date, not a contemporaneous public disclosure.

events.title: Puthoff and Targ report SRI remote-viewing experiments
events.summary: An SRI report covering January 1974 through February 1975 describes remote-viewing experiments and argues for useful information transfer.
events.significance: Lets readers compare the researchers’ original claims with later methodological and operational reviews.
established: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ authored the report and described laboratory and applied work.
limitations: These are the investigators’ claims. The excerpt is not an independent replication, and its anonymous subject codes are not converted into named participants here.

supports: authors, research period, goals and favorable interpretation

events.dateNotes: Date range is the research period printed on the report, not its exact issue date.

events.title: The Army consolidates intelligence functions in INSCOM
events.summary: The Army formed Intelligence and Security Command under a December 30, 1976 general order.
events.significance: Identifies the command on the later Gateway assessment.
established: NARA dates consolidation to January 1, 1977.
limitations: The command’s formation is not the start date of every later consciousness or remote-viewing project.

events.title: Voyager carries a message selected by Sagan’s committee
events.summary: The Voyager spacecraft launched with records representing life and culture on Earth. Carl Sagan chaired the selection committee.
events.significance: Shows an explicit scientific and cultural engagement with the possibility of extraterrestrial intelligence.
established: NASA documents the mission and Sagan’s selection role.
limitations: Sending a message does not establish that it was received, or that extraterrestrial life has been detected.
events.dateNotes: Year-level entry groups the two launches rather than assigning one spacecraft’s launch day to both.

events.title: The Department of Energy begins operations
events.summary: DOE became effective October 1 under the August 4 Department of Energy Organization Act.
events.significance: Places atomic administration within its later institutional structure.
established: NARA records the consolidation of ERDA, FEA and other functions.
limitations: DOE is not simply the AEC renamed; intermediate reorganizations matter.

supports: law, effective date and predecessor functions

events.dateNotes: Enabling law August 4; effective establishment October 1, 1977.

events.title: An Army officer assesses the Gateway Process
events.summary: Wayne McDonnell prepared an INSCOM assessment of Monroe’s Gateway training, proposing an account of its mechanisms and further experimentation.
events.significance: The surviving record makes an often-misidentified document available in its actual institutional context.
established: It is an Army-authored assessment preserved among CIA-released records.
limitations: Its speculative physical models and proposed experiments do not establish out-of-body perception, a new physics theory or NHI contact.

supports: author, date, Army provenance, stated task and conclusions

events.dateNotes: The report date is distinct from its September 10, 2003 release-approval stamp. That stamp is not treated as a verified first public-posting date.

events.title: The Air Force announces its Roswell assessment
events.summary: The Air Force said the recovered material was consistent with debris from a classified balloon project.
events.significance: Records the agency’s explanation separately from both the 1947 announcement and GAO’s later search.
established: NARA’s archival guidance preserves the date and the Air Force’s attributed conclusion.
limitations: An official assessment should be evaluated against its supporting records; the institutional conclusion alone does not answer every later claim.

events.title: GAO reports what its Roswell records search found
events.summary: GAO issued a report on its search for government records about the 1947 Roswell incident.
events.significance: Separates archival findings and gaps from theories offered to explain them.
established: The search found contemporary records and identified destroyed administrative files.
limitations: The destruction forms did not establish who destroyed the files or under what authority. That gap does not itself establish concealment of extraterrestrial evidence.

supports: report date, search findings and destruction-record limitation

events.title: Remote-viewing reviewers disagree about what the statistics show
events.summary: Ray Hyman’s dated assessment challenged Jessica Utts’s interpretation of the SRI/SAIC evidence.
events.significance: Preserves a substantive scientific disagreement rather than presenting a single government verdict.
established: Utts argued for anomalous cognition; Hyman accepted statistical departures in the reviewed work but required stronger independent replication before attributing them to a paranormal ability.
limitations: Statistical significance, causal mechanism and intelligence usefulness are separate claims.
events.dateNotes: September 11 dates Hyman’s evaluation; Utts’s standalone assessment is dated only to 1995 here. It is not a joint publication date.

events.title: AIR’s final review advises against intelligence use of remote viewing
events.summary: The CIA-commissioned AIR evaluation distinguished laboratory results from intelligence usefulness and recommended against continuation.
events.significance: Provides a direct record of the review’s methods, competing assessments and institutional recommendation.
established: AIR found statistical effects but no unambiguous paranormal cause; the operational review found no demonstrated actionable intelligence in the material it evaluated.
limitations: This is the reviewers’ conclusion about the reviewed program, not a proof that all conceivable consciousness effects are impossible. It is not itself a termination order.

supports: final-report date, scope, executive conclusions and recommendation

events.dateNotes: Final report September 29; a September 22 draft is a separate version. No exact declassification announcement or closure day is inferred from either.

events.title: A FOIA release adds detail to the CIA history of Area 51
events.summary: The National Security Archive published its account of a less-redacted CIA history of U-2 and OXCART reconnaissance.
events.significance: Offers a documented example of secrecy around human aircraft and a later, traceable disclosure.
established: The FOIA recipient identified newly visible names, locations and program details, including Groom Lake/Area 51.
limitations: The archive is nongovernmental. A real test site and classified aircraft do not authenticate claims of alien reverse engineering; the entire CIA history has not been independently audited here.

supports: recipient’s publication date, provenance and described changes

events.dateNotes: Release review approved June 25, 2013; the recipient’s public account is dated August 15.

events.title: Vallée begins donating research papers to Rice
events.summary: Rice’s finding aid dates the beginning of Jacques Vallée’s donations to December 2016.
events.significance: Creates a documented archival trail for a major UFO researcher while making access limits explicit.
established: The catalog describes correspondence, background files and notes, including material concerning NIDS and BAASS.
limitations: A finding aid is not access to the files or validation of their contents. The catalog lists separate future opening dates for restricted series.

supports: acquisition month, collection scope and access restrictions

events.dateNotes: Donation month is distinct from the collection’s 1960–2015 content dates and the finding aid’s 2019 date.

events.title: A dated retelling of the alleged 1933 Italian recovery
events.summary: An Italian report relayed Roberto Pinotti’s account of an alleged 1933 object recovery near Vergiate, often discussed as the Magenta story.
events.significance: Preserves the history of a consequential allegation without moving an unverified crash into the factual chronology.
established: The inspected article establishes that this account was publicly reported by March 2017.
limitations: No authenticated 1933 incident record, cabinet record or custody chain was inspected. Repeated stories drawing on Pinotti are not independent corroboration.

supports: dated publication and attribution to Pinotti

events.dateNotes: The article is a verified dated retelling, not the earliest-ever public account. Later Grusch statements do not retroactively authenticate the 1933 story.

claimDate.attribution: Roberto Pinotti’s account as retold in the inspected 2017 article
claimDate.note: Alleged incident date, not established fact; not used as this event’s sorting date.

events.title: The Monroe Institute describes McMoneagle’s role
events.summary: An institute post describes Joe McMoneagle as an Army remote viewer and recounts his work with Robert Monroe.
events.significance: Adds an inspectable institutional account for a central figure, with the author’s relationship disclosed.
established: The post documents what institute leadership said about McMoneagle and its training.
limitations: It was written by his spouse, Nancy McMoneagle. It does not independently establish claimed operational successes, near-death experiences or paranormal mechanisms.

supports: date, author, described roles and collaboration

events.dateNotes: The webpage publication is July 29 despite the title’s “August 2017.” No unsupported start date for the described collaboration is assigned.

events.title: An Army memo seeks human-use review of CENTER LANE
events.summary: INSCOM’s CENTER LANE project manager recommended review of the program’s protocol by its Human Technology Review Board.
events.significance: Separates named Army programs and their oversight history from the broader “Stargate” shorthand.
established: The memo says INSCOM GRILL FLAME activity ceased in September 1982 and psychoenergetic activity restarted under CENTER LANE in December 1982.
limitations: The memorandum’s administrative classifications and approvals do not establish that remote viewing worked. It is not an independent legal assessment of the entire program.

supports: date, author, recommendation and stated program transitions

events.dateNotes: The entry sorts on the memorandum date. Its account places the Army transition in December 1982; no invented day or universal start date for all programs is used.

events.title: Lazar’s anonymous television interview makes a recovery claim public
events.summary: KLAS aired an interview with Bob Lazar, using the name “Dennis,” alleging military study of alien technology in Nevada.
events.significance: A consequential moment in the public history of reverse-engineering allegations.
established: The broadcaster’s retrospective dates the interview and preserves excerpts of the claims, with reporting by George Knapp.
limitations: Broadcasting the claim does not establish Lazar’s claimed employment, a recovered craft or the described propulsion. Later Navy footage is not independent authentication of this story.

supports: original interview date, pseudonym, allegation and broadcaster attribution

events.dateNotes: Historical broadcast date comes from the broadcaster’s inspected retrospective. The later upload date remains separate.

changeLog.title: Initial source audit
changeLog.detail: Separated the December 16, 2017 online story from its December 17 print-front-page appearance. Earlier summaries are research leads, not sources.

changeLog.title: Removed an unsupported September 4 transfer date
changeLog.detail: NARA’s page-review date does not establish when additional agency collections arrived. The current eight-agency listing is described as a checked holding, not a newly dated transfer event.

changeLog.title: Narrowed the archive-procurement claim
changeLog.detail: Readable reporting supports an intended purchase, not an award. The previously stated July 31 notice date was not verified and is not used.

changeLog.title: Kept the waiver’s scope explicit
changeLog.detail: The announcement concerns specified communications to PURSUE. It is not described here as general permission for public disclosure.

changeLog.title: Added a historical NASA meeting
changeLog.detail: Added NASA’s May 31, 2023 public study meeting after inspecting the agency’s record. This is a historical addition, not a new incident or a finding about UAP origins.

changeLog.title: A historical layer, with provenance kept visible
changeLog.detail: Added selected historical milestones and a sourced people/programs index. Modern disclosure remains the default. The Maison Rouge report is an attributed intelligence account; UBC and BBH remain distinct; Gateway is Army-authored; Magenta sorts on a verified later retelling rather than an unverified 1933 crash. AIR’s final review is distinguished from its earlier draft. These are historical additions, not new incidents.
